title: Personal AML lab journal — day logs & quant notes
content:
Quick scratchpad for daily experiment notes, prompt candidates, and quantization heuristics. Not polished — mostly for my memory and next steps.

2026-03-10 — kick-off (short notes)
- Goal: cheap 4-bit variant for customer-demo workload (summarization + short Q&A). Keep latency < 120ms tail p95 for single-request small-batch.
- Baselines: hosted-mirror of mixtral-7b-v0 (fp16) => avg latency 95ms, p95 140ms (on dedicated gpus). Accuracy baseline: ROUGE-L 0.48 on demo set.
- Constraints: no FP16 fallback in private env; want quantized artifact that the private runtime can load (GPTQ-like).

Experiments run (notes):
1) mixtral-7b | GPTQ 4-bit | qgroup=64 | act-order:per-channel
   - compile: succeeded, model size ~3.1GB
   - perf: p50 48ms, p95 92ms (single request) on test node (A10G-like)
   - quality: ROUGE-L 0.44 (-8.3% vs fp16), hallucination rate up slightly (manual flagging).
   - observation: tokenization differences when using our tokenizer wrapper; need normalization step.

2) mixtral-7b | AWQ 4-bit (S4-like) | block=128
   - perf: p50 42ms, p95 80ms
   - quality: ROUGE-L 0.46 (-4.2%), better than GPTQ in short-answer coherence
   - regression: rare crashes when sequence length > 512 due to KV index overflow (workaround: pad to multiple of 64)

3) small ablation: caching prefix disabled vs enabled
   - enabled: latency p95 drops ~15-20% for repeated-conversation flows; cost per token reduced in steady-state
   - note: caching increases memory for batched concurrent sessions — need to estimate worst-case memory given 300 simultaneous sessions.

Quick table (rough)
- fp16 baseline: size 13GB | p95 140ms | ROUGE-L 0.48
- gptq-4: size 3.1GB | p95 92ms | ROUGE-L 0.44
- awq-4 (S4): size 3.0GB | p95 80ms | ROUGE-L 0.46

Prompts (demo set candidates)
- Summarize (short):
  Input: "{article}"
  Prompt: "Summarize the article in two concise bullet points with the key takeaway first."
  Expected style: explicit numeric bullets, 1-2 lines per bullet.

- Q&A (follow-up):
  Input: "{article}\nQuestion: What is the main limitation of the approach described?"
  Prompt: "Answer in 1-3 sentences. If unsure, say 'Insufficient information' instead of guessing."

- Safety guard: if answer contains phrases like 'I think' or 'probably', flag for review.

Notes on quant heuristics and compilation traps
- Always run standardized tokenization normalization before generating quant artifacts — whitespace/newline differences cause bigger quality deltas than expected.
- For GPTQ: use power-of-two group sizes where possible; non-uniform group sizes cause worse kernel selection on the runtime and degrades latency.
- AWQ/S4: observe better preservation of factuality on short summarization tasks; seems to preserve small weights better.
- Watch out for attention dtype casting bugs across runtime versions 1.12 -> 1.15 (we saw subtle NaN path on 1.15 when using fused-kernel). Add test harness.

Evaluation checklist (to formalize later)
- [ ] build stable eval harness for demo set (repeatable seed, 3 runs)
- [ ] add step to verify tokenization equivalence between quant pipeline and hosted tokenizer
- [ ] run memory worst-case calc for caching (300 sessions)
- [ ] add p95/p99 telemetry to console route for the demo config

2026-03-11 — follow-ups
- Re-ran AWQ with block=64 -> tiny perf regress (p95 +6ms) but slightly better ROUGE-L 0.461. Keep as candidate.
- Discovered file-format mismatch in the private deployment loader: model meta key 'rotary_dim' missing after conversion script v0.3. Patch ready in PR (see linked PR).

Quick todo (personal):
- [ ] push conversion patch to PR and link to internal QA job
- [ ] add tokenizer normalization step inside conversion tooling (lowercase/normalize unicode)
- [ ] schedule 30m sync with Lina to align on memory numbers (this week)
- [ ] bake a small script to compare outputs (gold vs quant) and extract top-3 tokens diffs per example

Open questions / weirdness to file:
- Why does GPTQ show larger hallucination drift on summary-adjacent tasks but preserved when doing directly extractive tasks? Hypothesis: per-group scaling artifacts amplify rare-token logits. Need to probe logits distribution.
- Is there a faster/safer fallback path integrated into private runtime for sequences>512? Right now I use pad-to-multiple workaround; should expose automated chunking.

2026-03-12 — short notes after run with demo harness
- Ran 3 seeds on AWQ block=64 candidate — stability looks OK, variance in ROUGE across seeds ~0.006.
- Latency looked stable p95 ~78-85ms on test node (still below demo threshold).
- Next: integrate into staging rollout (canary 5% traffic) and monitor token-level cost delta.

References and quick links (local):
- small compare script: /home/noah/repo/aml-tools/compare-quant.sh (TODO: push to repo)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rlhf-experiments/pull/214 (conversion patch)
- JIRA: JIRA-AML-678 (memory/caching estimation)

Random notes to self:
- If pivot to 3-bit quant, prioritize AWQ path; do small smoke test first.
- Add a short README for engineers: 'how to sanity-check a quant model before shipping' — include tokenizer-check, basic eval, crash-patterns.

End of scratch for now. Will formalize into a PR summary once canary metrics look clean.
